heroHeadline: HRW: Russia's Africa Corps Summarily Killed 9 Civilians, Including 4 Children, in Bombori Raid; Bamako Blockade at Day 114
heroSubtitle: Human Rights Watch reported August 20, 2026 that more than 100 Russian Africa Corps fighters, escorted by 4 Malian soldiers, raided the Fulani neighborhood of Bombori village (Mopti Region) on July 10, killing 9 civilians including 4 children, beating dozens more among 80+ detained, and burning 8 homes — HRW's second documented Africa Corps civilian-harm incident in six weeks, after the June 15 Kyrnia airstrike (8 killed, reported July 31). HRW senior Sahel researcher Ilaria Allegrozzi said 'the Malian junta appears to have given Russian Africa Corps forces a green light to kill civilians'; Russian and Malian defense ministries did not respond to HRW's August 4-5 inquiries. ACTIVE FRONTS (Aug 20): (1) BAMAKO BLOCKADE (Day 114 since the April 28 'total siege' declaration): assessed as 'tightening, not thawing' — 300+ fuel tankers destroyed and 1,000+ convoys escorted since the blockade began; JNIM extended its reach further south with the Aug 9 assault on FAMa's barracks in San, Ségou Region (10+ soldiers killed), well below the historical northern front line. (2) FUNDING & LOGISTICS: A UN sanctions report (Reuters, Aug 14) found a ~$50M ransom paid in 2025, allegedly by the UAE, helped finance JNIM's 2026 Mali offensive; C4ADS flight-tracking (Aug 13) documented 75 Russian military/military-linked flights to Africa Corps bases in Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger since January 2025. (3) BURKINA FASO: government territory-control claims (74.53%, per the Ministry of Defense) remain sharply contested against independent estimates (~40%, Africa Center); the #2 and #3 junta officials remain absent from public view amid an unconfirmed power-struggle report. (4) HUMANITARIAN: the Sahel recorded 9,928 militant-Islamist-violence deaths in the 12 months to mid-2026 (Africa Center, Aug 12) — 42% of Africa's continental total, with JNIM responsible for roughly 76% of regional deaths.
